_why: HOW THIS ESTATE WRITES DOWN THAT SOMEBODY IS ALIVE, in one place, because three
separate readers of the same question each missed the same person.
Tersia Booyzen is recorded b = "living" in the Booyzen archive — the archive
stating she is alive in the field a birth date would occupy, with no boolean
anywhere. checkliving.py read living FLAGS and counted zero. The kit's chart
helper rendered «b. living» as though it were a date. And register.astro
published, in bold, «No living person is in this register, and none is anywhere
in this archive: of the 354 people it holds, not one is living» — which is false
about a living woman, on the one rule this estate treats as absolute.
Three readers, three languages, one blind spot, and each agreed with the others
for the same wrong reason. Two implementations agreeing is evidence only when
they CAN disagree; these could not. So the vocabulary is declared here and read
rather than restated, and a fourth reader cannot quietly know less than the gate.
